I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for Left Atrial Appendage Closure (LAAC) using the Watchman FLX / Amulet device for my patient. This procedure is medically necessary and is supported by the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Atrial Fibrillation, multiple randomized controlled trials, and CMS coverage policy NCD 20.34.

EVIDENCE-BASED JUSTIFICATION:

1. 2023 ACC/AHA GUIDELINE SUPPORT:
Per the 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation (Joglar JA, et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2024;83:109-279), LAAC is a Class IIa recommendation for patients with AF and high stroke risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥2) who have contraindications to long-term oral anticoagulation. This patient meets these criteria.

2. RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL EVIDENCE:
The PROTECT AF trial (Holmes DR, et al., Lancet 2009;374:534-542) and PREVAIL trial (Holmes DR, et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2014;64:1-12) demonstrated that LAAC with the Watchman device is non-inferior to warfarin for stroke prevention in non-valvular AF, with a favorable long-term bleeding profile after the initial post-procedure antiplatelet period.

The PRAGUE-17 trial (Osmancik P, et al., J Am Coll Cardiol 2020;75:3122-3135) demonstrated that LAAC is non-inferior to DOAC therapy for the composite endpoint of stroke, cardiovascular death, and major bleeding, with significantly lower rates of non-procedural bleeding.

[IF PRIOR ICH]: For patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, LAAC is the preferred stroke prevention strategy over anticoagulation, as the risk of recurrent ICH on anticoagulation (3–8% per year) far exceeds the procedural risk of LAAC (<2% major complications in experienced centers).

3. CMS COVERAGE POLICY:
This patient meets all criteria under CMS NCD 20.34 for LAAC coverage:
✓ Non-valvular atrial fibrillation
✓ CHA₂DS₂-VASc score ≥2
✓ Documented contraindication to long-term anticoagulation
✓ Structural heart team evaluation completed
✓ Pre-procedure TEE confirmed no LAA thrombus

4. PRE-PROCEDURE EVALUATION:

• Structural heart team evaluation: {{letter_date}} — LAAC recommended

The risk of stroke without treatment significantly outweighs the procedural risk of LAAC in an experienced structural heart center.
